question: Is a yield line mandatory at every roundabout entrance under Section 3D.04?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. Under Section 3D.04, a yield line at a roundabout entrance is an Option, not a requirement — it "may be used to indicate the point behind which vehicles are required to yield at the entrance to a roundabout" (see [Image 3]). What is mandatory at roundabout entrances is the YIELD sign itself, per the Standard in Section 2B.10; the pavement markings (yield line, YIELD word marking, dotted edge line extension) are recommended or permitted, not required. Standards (mandatory): - "A YIELD sign shall be used to require road users to yield the right-of-way to other traffic at the entrance to a roundabout. YIELD signs at roundabouts shall be used to control the approach roadways and shall not be used to control the circulatory roadway." - "YIELD signs shall not be placed on all of the approaches to an intersection, except at roundabouts." Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, it should be: "A. A solid line adjacent to the splitter island, and B. A wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout" (see Figure 3D-1) — this is recommended practice, not a yield line requirement. Options (permitted): - Per Section 3D.04 (Option): "A yield line (see Section 3B.19) may be used to indicate the point behind which vehicles are required to yield at the entrance to a roundabout (see Figures 3D-1 and 3D-2)." (text visible in [Image 3]) - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows roundabout approach markings, with the YIELD word marking and yield line elements labeled "Optional" and the "Wide dotted white extension of circulatory roadway edge line" called out. - [Image 2] Figure 3D-2 illustrates a one-lane roundabout where yield-related markings (yield lines and YIELD word markings) are flagged with the "Optional" asterisk in the legend. - [Image 3] shows the text of Section 3D.04, confirming the yield line appears only under the "Option" heading ("may be used"), not under a Standard. - [Image 4] is the full-page view of Figure 3D-1, again labeling the yield line and YIELD word markings as "Optional." - [Image 5] shows the Chapter 3D text including Section 3D.03, where the wide dotted line across entering lanes is stated as Guidance ("should"). - [Image 6] shows Figure 3D-3 (Sheet 1), where yield line markings on approaches carry the optional asterisk in the legend. Citations: - Section 2B.10 Standard §5 (p.78) - Section 2B.10 Standard §6 (p.78) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596) - Figure 3D-2 (p.597) - Page 646
gold_answer: No. A yield line may be used to indicate the point behind which vehicles are required to yield at a roundabout entrance; it is an Option, not a universal requirement.
